Storage Manager (SM) is the CMS online system at P5 that manages the lifecycle of HLT “streamer” files (the RAW data) between P5 and Tier‑0. What it does - Orchestrates the official transfer of streamer files from P5 to Tier‑0; Tier‑0 only handles data delivered via SM. - Keeps bookkeeping and enforces the directory/transfer protocol for new runs and streams. - Monitors Tier‑0 repacking status and, once it’s safe, deletes the corresponding files from the P5 storage to keep occupancy under control. Why it matters - Protects RAW data integrity (won’t delete at P5 until repack is confirmed). - Prevents P5 storage from filling up by cleaning promptly after safe transfer. - Ensures Tier‑0 only ingests data that followed the validated online→offline path. Notes from ops tickets - “Only the data transferred by the SM will be handled” by Tier‑0 (CMSTZ‑1071). - SM uses Tier‑0 repack status to decide when it’s safe to delete P5 data (CMSTZ‑1081). If you need details on a specific run/stream or SM→Tier‑0 transfers, tell me the run/stream and timeframe. ---

Tier0Feeder is the Tier‑0 agent component that “feeds” new data and configuration into Tier‑0. How do I create a new Tier0 release

Here’s the short, operator-focused procedure to create a new Tier‑0 (T0) release. Prerequisites - Access vocms055 (CC7 RPM build VM) and join the cms-comp-devs e-group (so you can upload to your personal cmsrep). Ask CMSWEB operator if you don’t have them. - On vocms055, set up build env: - Create /build/. - Clone pkgtools (checkout V00-32-XX). - Clone cms-sw/cmsdist (use the comp_gcc630 branch; verify current branch with CMSWEB ops). Build and upload a testable RPM from your fork - Create a new GitHub release tag in dmwm/T0 (fork if needed; tag sequentially, e.g. 3.0.7 → 3.0.8). - Edit cmsdist/t0.spec in your local cmsdist clone: - Bump the T0 version to your new tag. - Set WMCore version: %define wmcver X.Y.Z (match what you intend to run). - For testing from your fork, point Source0 to your repo, e.g. git://github.com//T0.git?obj=master/%{realversion}&export=T0-%{realversion}&output=/T0-%{realversion}.tar.gz - Build and upload to your personal cmsrep: - cmsBuild … build t0 - cmsBuild … upload t0 --upload-user=$USER Test the release on a replay node - On the replay node under /data/tier0: - In 00_deploy_replay.sh (and/or 00_deploy_*.sh): - Set TIER0_VERSION to your tag. - Use your personal repo: -r comp=comp.. - Update /data/tier0/admin/ReplayOfflineConfiguration.py to the latest intended config. - Fully stop the agent; then run 00_deploy_replay.sh and start the agent; run a replay. - Verify components and workflow creation; ensure the replay is healthy. - Note: 00_deploy* wipes the T0AST DB. Do not run on production by mistake. Make it an official CMS release - From your local T0 repo, generate changelog and tag via bin/buildrelease.sh (e.g. . bin/buildrelease.sh --skip-build --wmcore-tag= ), then push tags to your fork and upstream. - Open a PR to cms-sw/cmsdist updating only t0.spec to your new release version (and WMCore if needed). - Ask WMCore/CMSWEB devs to force-merge into the active comp_* branch (Tier0 doesn’t follow the monthly cycle). - Wait for the official build to appear in the comp repo (cmsrep comp/slc7_amd64_gcc630). Verify availability. - Update the Tier0 release notes on the T0AST/T0 production twiki. Add any subsequent patch notes. Deploy in production - Update deployment variables on the production node(s): TIER0_VERSION and DEPLOY_TAG to the new official release. - Perform a standard prod deploy, start the agent, and verify health. If you want, tell me your target tag and WMCore version and I can draft the exact t0.spec changes and the cmsBuild/upload commands for your user. ---

question: Why is prompt reconstruction not ran by central production?
history: I’m Archi, the CMS CompOps assistant. I don’t see personal details about you, only that you’re logged in with the role: base-user. If you meant something else (e.g., your CERN account name, Grid DN, or service roles), tell me what you want to check and I’ll guide you.

Storage Manager (SM) is the CMS online system at P5 that manages the lifecycle of HLT “streamer” files (the RAW data) between P5 and Tier‑0. What it does - Orchestrates the official transfer of streamer files from P5 to Tier‑0; Tier‑0 only handles data delivered via SM. - Keeps bookkeeping and enforces the directory/transfer protocol for new runs and streams. - Monitors Tier‑0 repacking status and, once it’s safe, deletes the corresponding files from the P5 storage to keep occupancy under control. Why it matters - Protects RAW data integrity (won’t delete at P5 until repack is confirmed). - Prevents P5 storage from filling up by cleaning promptly after safe transfer. - Ensures Tier‑0 only ingests data that followed the validated online→offline path. Notes from ops tickets - “Only the data transferred by the SM will be handled” by Tier‑0 (CMSTZ‑1071). - SM uses Tier‑0 repack status to decide when it’s safe to delete P5 data (CMSTZ‑1081). If you need details on a specific run/stream or SM→Tier‑0 transfers, tell me the run/stream and timeframe. ---

Tier0Feeder is the Tier‑0 agent component that “feeds” new data and configuration into Tier‑0. It polls Storage Manager for newly available streamer files, sets up runs/streams/datasets, and creates the corresponding Tier‑0 workflows. What it does - Polls Storage Manager and injects new streamer files into the Tier‑0 database (T0AST); notifies SM that files were seen (file_transfer_status_offline). - Retrieves CMSSW version and HLT key for new runs (via CMS_HLT_R) and records runs/streams in T0AST. - Configures new runs and streams according to the Tier‑0 configuration (ProdOfflineConfiguration.py or ReplayOfflineConfiguration.py). - Creates the Repack and Express workflows and subscriptions in WMBS/DBSBuffer; updates T0 Data Service tables. - Manages the Conditions Upload procedure for runs. - Marks workflows as injected when PromptReco for the run is released, preventing premature cleanup. Operational notes - The main loop is implemented by the Tier0FeederPoller. - Each deployment has a DeploymentID (file under …/Tier0Feeder/DeploymentID.txt) used to track replays in Grafana/WMStats. If you want, tell me a run/stream and I can help check whether Tier0Feeder injected it and created the workflows. ---

How do I create a new Tier0 release

Here’s the short, operator-focused procedure to create a new Tier‑0 (T0) release. Prerequisites - Access vocms055 (CC7 RPM build VM) and join the cms-comp-devs e-group (so you can upload to your personal cmsrep). Ask CMSWEB operator if you don’t have them. - On vocms055, set up build env: - Create /build/. - Clone pkgtools (checkout V00-32-XX). - Clone cms-sw/cmsdist (use the comp_gcc630 branch; verify current branch with CMSWEB ops). Build and upload a testable RPM from your fork - Create a new GitHub release tag in dmwm/T0 (fork if needed; tag sequentially, e.g. 3.0.7 → 3.0.8). - Edit cmsdist/t0.spec in your local cmsdist clone: - Bump the T0 version to your new tag. - Set WMCore version: %define wmcver X.Y.Z (match what you intend to run). - For testing from your fork, point Source0 to your repo, e.g. git://github.com//T0.git?obj=master/%{realversion}&export=T0-%{realversion}&output=/T0-%{realversion}.tar.gz - Build and upload to your personal cmsrep: - cmsBuild … build t0 - cmsBuild … upload t0 --upload-user=$USER Test the release on a replay node - On the replay node under /data/tier0: - In 00_deploy_replay.sh (and/or 00_deploy_*.sh): - Set TIER0_VERSION to your tag. - Use your personal repo: -r comp=comp.. - Update /data/tier0/admin/ReplayOfflineConfiguration.py to the latest intended config. - Fully stop the agent; then run 00_deploy_replay.sh and start the agent; run a replay. - Verify components and workflow creation; ensure the replay is healthy. - Note: 00_deploy* wipes the T0AST DB. Do not run on production by mistake. Make it an official CMS release - From your local T0 repo, generate changelog and tag via bin/buildrelease.sh (e.g. . bin/buildrelease.sh --skip-build --wmcore-tag= ), then push tags to your fork and upstream. - Open a PR to cms-sw/cmsdist updating only t0.spec to your new release version (and WMCore if needed). - Ask WMCore/CMSWEB devs to force-merge into the active comp_* branch (Tier0 doesn’t follow the monthly cycle). - Wait for the official build to appear in the comp repo (cmsrep comp/slc7_amd64_gcc630). Verify availability. - Update the Tier0 release notes on the T0AST/T0 production twiki. Add any subsequent patch notes. Deploy in production - Update deployment variables on the production node(s): TIER0_VERSION and DEPLOY_TAG to the new official release. - Perform a standard prod deploy, start the agent, and verify health. If you want, tell me your target tag and WMCore version and I can draft the exact t0.spec changes and the cmsBuild/upload commands for your user. ---

What are monte carlo workflows in Tier-0

Short answer: Tier‑0 does not run Monte Carlo production. Tier‑0 is for prompt processing of real detector data from P5 (Repack, Express, PromptReco, skims/harvesting). Where Monte Carlo runs - Central production handles MC via McM → ReqMgr2/Global WorkQueue → WMAgents at Tier‑1/2 sites (orchestrated by Unified). In WMCore terms “MonteCarlo” workflows have no input data and are split by requested events—not something Tier‑0 does. Notes - You may see MC used in replays or small tests to validate Tier‑0 configurations, but that’s not Tier‑0 production. - If you meant RelVals or PCL tests touching Tier‑0, say which context and I can detail that path. ---

history: A CMS user needs to extend his user quota at my site (T2_CN_Beijing) in Rucio. Actually I don't know how to do this. Is there any wiki or application webpage I could follow?

Short answer: there are two different “quotas” people usually mean, and the way to change them is different. 1) Site (RSE) total quota for CMS at your site - What it is: how much disk Rucio is allowed to use at T2_CN_Beijing overall (central ops + local use). - How to change it: use the SiteCapacity web app and update your site’s values. Rucio will pick it up automatically within ~1 hour. - App: https://cmssst.web.cern.ch/cgi-bin/set/SiteCapacity - Tip: The Rucio quota is the sum of “Disk space in TBytes available for experiment central operations” and “Disk space in TBytes available for local use.” - Verify after sync: rucio-admin rse info T2_CN_Beijing - Reference: internal doc “disk_quota_management.md” and CMSDM ticket examples show this workflow. 2) Per-user (Rucio account) quota at your site (local account limit) - What it is: a limit for a specific Rucio account at a specific RSE (e.g., a CMS user hitting “AccountLimitExceeded” at T2_CN_Beijing). - Who can change it: CMS Rucio admins (typically DM experts), not regular site admins. - How it’s changed: a CMS Rucio admin runs something like: - rucio-admin account set-limits T2_CN_Beijing - Example (5 PB): rucio-admin account set-limits someuser T2_CN_Beijing 5000000000000000 - What you can do: - Ask the user for their Rucio account name and how much they need. - Open a CMSDM JIRA ticket (category: Data Management/Rucio) requesting a per-account limit change at T2_CN_Beijing, or ping the DM experts. - Users can check their own limits with: rucio list-account-limits Useful links - SiteCapacity app (to change site/RSE quota): https://cmssst.web.cern.ch/cgi-bin/set/SiteCapacity - RSE quotas overview page: https://cmsdatapop.web.cern.ch/cmsdatapop/rucio/quotas.html If you’re unsure which quota is the problem, ask the user for the exact Rucio error. “AccountLimitExceeded” with their account name means the per-user (local account) limit; “RSE is full” or no space left typically points to the site/RSE total quota. ---

history: there are a lot of unmerged files at rail t1 and t2. which service is responsible to deleting those, are they even delted, give me monitorign links

Short answer - Responsible service: MSUnmerged (ReqMgr2 Microservice). Cleanup jobs in the workflows do a first pass; MSUnmerged is the continuous/central cleanup for leftover /store/unmerged files at T1/T2 RSEs. - Are they deleted? Yes, when they’re no longer needed (after protection windows and safety checks). If you still see a lot, it’s usually because they’re still protected, the site is temporarily rejecting deletions, or there is backlog/throttling. Monitoring/inspection links (require CERN X509 cert) - RAL T1 (T1_UK_RAL_Disk) detailed unmerged status: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/ms-unmerged/data/info?rse=T1_UK_RAL_Disk&detail=true - RAL T2 (T2_UK_SGrid_RALPP) detailed unmerged status: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/ms-unmerged/data/info?rse=T2_UK_SGrid_RALPP&detail=true - MSUnmerged service status (T1 replica): https://cmsweb.cern.ch/ms-unmerged/data/status?rse_type=t1 - MSUnmerged service status (T2/T3 replica): https://cmsweb.cern.ch/ms-unmerged/data/status?rse_type=t2t3 - Summary for all tracked RSEs: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/ms-unmerged/data/info?rse=ALL_DOCS&detail=false Notes - These endpoints return JSON with what was protected, scheduled-to-delete, deleted, failed, and timestamps of the last cycle. - Deletions of /store/unmerged are site-local (not via Rucio), so you won’t see them in Rucio deletion events. - If RAL isn’t the site you meant by “rail,” tell me which T1/T2 and I’ll give you the exact RSE links. ---

history: On Feb 24th, why the CPU efficiency was so low in FNAL?

Short answer: it was driven by I/O‑bound workloads and evictions, not a sitewide CPU problem.

What I see for 2026‑02‑24 (UTC) at T1_US_FNAL:
- Overall avg CPU efficiency: 61.6%. The “low efficiency” came from large pockets of jobs with CpuEff < 50%.
- Offsite reads were poor: avg CpuEff 31.1% for InputData=Offsite vs 61.9% for Onsite.
- Low‑efficiency jobs were dominated by Production and Analysis:
  - By job type (within CpuEff<50): Production ~209k, Analysis ~155k (top workflows included BPH‑RunIII2024Summer24GS‑00068, GEN‑Run3Summer22EEwmLHEGS‑00740, SMP‑RunIII2024Summer24wmLHEGS‑00157, etc.).
- Evictions/preemptions contributed to wasted wall time:
  - Avg NumVacates for low‑eff jobs: 1.58 (sitewide avg 1.28).
  - Exit reasons among low‑eff jobs frequently “died on signal 9 (Killed)”.
- Many of the low‑eff jobs were 1‑core and short, where fixed overheads/stage‑in dominate:
  - Within CpuEff<50: RequestCpus=1 had avg CpuEff ~14.6% (multi‑core >1 cpu ~18.2%).
- For low‑efficiency Onsite jobs the average WallClock was long (~11.3 h), consistent with I/O throttling/idle waits (e.g., storage contention), further depressing CpuEff.

Best guess at root cause on Feb 24:
- A workload mix heavy in short Analysis/GEN/GS tasks plus significant Offsite data access (poor locality), combined with elevated evictions and probable storage I/O contention, led to substantial wall time not spent on CPU, hence the dip in CPU efficiency at FNAL.

If you meant a different Feb 24 (year), tell me which year and I’ll re-run the check.

Hello, a CRAB user is asking this:

Dear computing expert,

I sent some crab jobs last Wednesday; most of them (80%) ran and finished fine. Since then, the jobs proceed at an abysmal speed. I have <10 running jobs with thousands of jobs either in idle or unsubmitted. In the last 48h the completion percentage moved less than 0.5%.

Is it a quota issue? Site issue? What can I do to improve the situation? The jobs are extremely urgent due to approval deadlines for winter conferences.

I can provide logs or other material if useful. Example of a crab status that does not really evolve:

```
Task name: 260311_183215:abragagn_crab_data_Run2025C_v1_part1_2026Mar11
Jobs status: finished 29.9% (1005/3363)
idle 31.3% (1052/3363)
running 0.0% ( 1/3363)
toRetry 0.1% ( 3/3363)
transferring 0.3% ( 9/3363)
unsubmitted 38.4% (1293/3363)
```

Thanks,
Alberto

Short answer: it’s not a CRAB “quota” problem on your side; it’s data‑locality plus site pressure. Most of your idle jobs are constrained to 1–2 sites that hold the data, and those sites have little analysis capacity right now, so matchmaking barely starts anything. You can speed things up by allowing remote read (AAA) and widening the site set. What I checked - Your tasks are visible in HTCondor monitoring. Example: - abragagn_crab_data_Run2025C_v1_part1_2026Mar11 jobs are Idle for many hours with DESIRED_Sites = [T1_UK_RAL, T2_US_Vanderbilt], i.e. only 1× T1 + 1× T2. That’s very restrictive and explains the long Idle times. - For other parts, I see DESIRED_Sites constrained to Tier‑1s (e.g. T1_IT_CNAF, T1_US_FNAL) or small pairs (e.g. T1_IT_CNAF, T1_PL_NCBJ). Again, very few places to run. - Where a dataset has replicas at T1_US_FNAL/T1_FR_CCIN2P3 (e.g. part7), I see jobs completing at FNAL with good CPU efficiency. So when the data is at a big site, you do make progress; when it’s at a tiny set (e.g. RAL + Vanderbilt), you stall. - The large “unsubmitted” fraction in crab status is normal: the TaskWorker throttles submissions while many jobs are already Idle; it increases as the schedd/queue frees up. Why this happens - You are running with locality (Onsite) so jobs only match where the MINIAOD blocks sit. Some of your blocks appear to be at only 1–2 sites that are currently saturated for analysis. That’s why progress has nearly flat‑lined. What you can do now (to get throughput back) - Allow remote read and widen where the jobs can run: - In your CRAB config: - config.Data.ignoreLocality = True - Optionally set a broad whitelist of good AAA sites, e.g. Tier‑1s and reliable Tier‑2s: T2_CH_CERN, T2_DE_DESY, T2_FR_GRIF_LLR, T2_IT_Bari, T2_IT_Pisa, T2_ES_CIEMAT, T2_UK_London_IC, T2_US_Caltech, T2_US_Nebraska, T2_US_Wisconsin, T1_*_Disk - Keep your current memory/cores. - This lets jobs run where there are slots and read via AAA from the data‑hosting site. For MINIAOD this usually works well. Given your urgency, this is the fastest lever. - If you want to keep Onsite for some tasks, replicate a few busiest blocks to a high‑capacity site (e.g. CERN) via a short‑lived Rucio rule using your analysis account/quota. Short answer: the jobs are idle/unsubmitted because the input data isn’t on disk at any eligible site. CRAB has requested a disk replica via CMS DDM (Rucio), and until that replication completes there’s no match-making, so the task stays Idle/Unsubmitted. Why I think this is the case - This exact symptom for CRAB analysis tasks almost always comes from data locality: the dataset (or a parent dataset if useParent=True) is tape-only or lacks a disk copy at analysis sites. We’ve seen identical reports where crab status shows “A disk replica has been requested to CMS DDM …” and nothing runs until the replica appears on disk. - When that happens, CRAB/GlideinWMS won’t submit/run jobs because DESIRED_Sites can’t be satisfied. What to check/confirm - Run crab status on the task: if you see the DDM replica message, that confirms it. - Look in DAS/Rucio for the dataset and verify there are no disk replicas (only T1_*_Tape or no eligible disk RSEs). - If useParent=True, check the parent dataset’s disk availability too. How to unblock - Ask Data Management to place a disk replica for the dataset at analysis-capable sites (we can open/boost a Rucio rule if you share the dataset name and preferred sites). - If WAN reads are acceptable and the input is small, consider ignoreLocality = True (not generally recommended for large AOD/RAW reads). - Widen the site whitelist if the replica exists but only at sites outside the current whitelist. If you share the CRAB task name (crab_), the input dataset(s), and whether useParent=True, I can verify the Rucio rule status and where the replication is stuck, and propose a concrete target site for the replica. ---

history: Please find documentation for PnR Campaign manager responsibilities and explain to me the meaning of `partial_copy` parameter

Here’s the documentation and the meaning of partial_copy. Where to read the responsibilities - Campaign Manager responsibilities (PnR/CompOps): https://cmspnr.docs.cern.ch/devoperator_responsibilities/campaign_manager - In short: - Monitor the PRCAMPAIGNS JIRA project daily (triage and follow up). - Make campaign changes when necessary (per PdmV/TSG requests). - Sync approved changes into the relevant configs/databases. Meaning of partial_copy - Field name: - Unified/CompOps config key: partial_copy - WMCore/MSMonitor name: PartialCopy - What it controls: - It is the required input staging fraction for a campaign. - Used by WMCore MicroService MSMonitor to decide the “staging → staged” transition for requests in that campaign. - Type and default: - Float in [0.0–1.0], default 1.0 (i.e., require 100% of the intended input to be staged). - How to interpret: - 1.0: wait until all required input is staged before the request is considered staged. - 0.95: proceed once 95% of the required input is staged (useful to avoid being blocked by a small tail). - Very low values (e.g., 0.05) are typically a misconfiguration and may cause jobs to start with most input missing. - Related notes: - “Used by” in docs: WMCore/MSMonitor (not MSTransferor). - Sometimes referred to as “InputFractionPass” or “minInputFraction” in discussions. - Choose values <1.0 only when acceptable to start running with a small fraction of input still transferring; coordinate with PdmV when this affects physics output (e.g., PU/MB secondaries). Examples seen in PRCAMPAIGNS tickets (for context) - partial_copy: 0.95 in PRCAMPAIGNS-132 (allow early start after most input is staged) - partial_copy set to 0.99 requested in PRCAMPAIGNS-151 (tight but allows ignoring the last ~1%) - partial_copy: 0.05 flagged in PRCAMPAIGNS-493 (too low; likely to cause issues) Source - Campaign Manager doc (includes the configuration table with partial_copy): https://cmspnr.docs.cern.ch/devoperator_responsibilities/campaign_manager - Table entry: “partial_copy (WMCore: PartialCopy) — Specifies the required input staging fraction of the given campaign; default 1.0; used by WMCore/MSMonitor for the staging→staged transition.” ---

What to do now 1) Immediate recall + pin on disk - Identify the datasets: - /EGamma*/Run2026A-EcalUncalWElectron-PromptReco-v*/ALCARECO - /EGamma*/Run2026A-EcalUncalZElectron-PromptReco-v*/ALCARECO - And the same for already-produced 2026B (since they’re getting deleted): - /EGamma*/Run2026B-EcalUncal[WZ]Electron-PromptReco-v*/ALCARECO - For each matching dataset, add a 1-copy rule to a CERN disk RSE (usually T2_CH_CERN) with 365-day lifetime. Example CLI (adjust account to your central one, typically cms): - rucio list-dids cms:'/EGamma*/Run2026A-EcalUncal[WZ]Electron-PromptReco-v*/ALCARECO' --did-type=dataset - For each DID X, add: - rucio add-rule cms:"X" 1 T2_CH_CERN --lifetime 31536000 --account cms --activity "Data Consolidation" --comment "CMSTRANSF-1322 ECAL ALCARECO 2026" - Why this solves it: - If the only copy is on tape, Rucio will recall the files onto disk as part of satisfying the rule. - The 1‑year lifetime prevents cleanup from deleting the disk copy during 2026. 2) Put automation in place so future eras (2026C, D, …) stay on disk automatically - Use the proposed regex pattern to cover W and Z skims across 2026 eras: - ^/EGamma[0-9]/Run2026[A-Z]-EcalUncal[WZ]Electron-PromptReco-v[0-9]+/ALCARECO$ - Note: If there can also be a plain “EGamma” (no digit) stream, consider expanding to: - ^/EGamma([0-9])?/Run2026[A-Z]-EcalUncal[WZ]Electron-PromptReco-v[0-9]+/ALCARECO$ - Two ways to automate: a) Rucio subscription (requires appropriate privileges): - rucio add-subscription 'ECAL_ALCARECO_2026_skims_CMSTRANSF-1322' cms \ '{"scope":"cms","project":"data","datatype":"ALCARECO","pattern":"^/EGamma([0-9])?/Run2026[A-Z]-EcalUncal[WZ]Electron-PromptReco-v[0-9]+/ALCARECO$"}' \ '[{"copies":1,"rse_expression":"T2_CH_CERN","lifetime":31536000,"activity":"Data Consolidation","comment":"CMSTRANSF-1322"}]' b) If we’re using the CMS AlCa auto-rules list (per CMSTRANSF-899/TWiki), add this exact regex there with target RSE T2_CH_CERN and lifetime 365 days, then deploy the change. - Post the subscription ID or the reference to the auto-rules change in the JIRA, plus the rule IDs you created for 2026A/B. 3) Sanity checks and follow-up - Space/quota: Verify cms account quota at T2_CH_CERN is sufficient for these datasets. If not, consider T1_CH_CERN_Disk or a small CERN+fallback expression (e.g., T2_CH_CERN|T1_CH_CERN_Disk). - Monitor transfers: rucio list-rules cms:"X" to get rule_id; then use Rucio/FTS monitoring via data.transfer_link if needed. - Confirm deletion stops: Once the rules are in place, the datasets should no longer be deleted; reply on the ticket with rule IDs and ETA for completion. If you confirm the target RSE (T2_CH_CERN vs T1_CH_CERN_Disk) and whether we should include plain “EGamma” (no digit) in the regex, I can draft the exact commands and the regex you want to commit to the automation. ---
